page.title: Best video doorbell with no subscription (2026): Tapo D225, AOSU Pro, eufy E340 compared
page.h1: Best video doorbell with no subscription
page.desc: Five battery doorbells that record without a monthly fee, compared on where clips are stored, real battery life, chime and Wi-Fi. Prices checked 2026-11-06.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best video doorbell with no subscription for most homes is the TP-Link Tapo D225 (sold by TP-Link and on Amazon; we do not link it): $89.99 on tp-link.com on 2026-11-06, a 10,000 mAh battery rated for 8 months, a microSD slot up to 512 GB and a chime in the box. If you want the clips kept inside the house instead of inside the doorbell, the AOSU Video Doorbell Pro ({buy:aosu-video-doorbell-pro}) wins: its included aosuBase Mini is the chime, the Wi-Fi extender and the recorder (add a microSD card up to 128 GB), with a 180-day battery claim. The number one owner complaint on every no-fee doorbell is recharging: eufy E340 owners report 2 weeks to 2 months per charge, and AOSU's own forum says the 180-day figure assumes 3 to 5 short events a day, so expect 2 to 4 months at a normal front door.

All five doorbells below record, play back, alert and talk without a plan. The paid tiers only add cloud backup and extras such as package or face recognition. What separates them is where the clips live, how often you climb a ladder to recharge, whether a chime is in the box, and whether the doorbell can reach your router.

page.after:
What owners complain about

We read AOSU's and eufy's community forums, TP-Link's support forum, Best Buy and Lowe's reviews, a SmartHomeScene teardown review and an r/smarthome thread on subscription-free doorbells. The same five problems kept coming up.

  • Battery life far under the claim (most frequent, 9 reports). An AOSU owner got about 2 months from a 180-day doorbell at one event a day; AOSU staff replied that the rating assumes 3 to 5 short events a day, warm weather and a Wi-Fi signal better than -65 dBm. eufy E340 owners report 33 days in one measured test, 17 days at a Lowe's reviewer's door and 50% gone in a week on a busy road. Tapo D225 owners on TP-Link's forum report batteries draining even when hardwired.
  • Slow notifications and live view (6 reports). A eufy owner's colleagues wait 5 seconds or more to talk to a visitor; AOSU owners say live view can take a while to load after an alert.
  • Weak Wi-Fi at the door (5 reports). Most battery doorbells are 2.4 GHz only and sit on the far side of an exterior wall. AOSU's base and eufy's HomeBase act as bridges; Tapo and Reolink talk straight to the router.
  • Where the clips go (4 reports). The E340's 8 GB is fixed and sits in the doorbell; a microSD card in a Tapo or Reolink doorbell leaves with the doorbell if it is pried off. Only the two AOSU doorbells put the recorder indoors at this price.
  • No chime in the box (3 reports). eufy and Reolink owners found out after mounting that a chime or a smart speaker is extra.

Which one by need

  • Longest battery and most storage for the money: Tapo D225. The 10,000 mAh cell is the biggest here, the card slot takes 512 GB, and it records 24/7 when wired. Weak spots are 2.4 GHz only and the hardwired battery-drain threads.
  • Recordings kept indoors with a chime, under $100: AOSU Video Doorbell Pro. The aosuBase Mini is the chime, the Wi-Fi extender and the recorder; buy a microSD card up to 128 GB with it. Expect 2 to 4 months per charge at a normal door.
  • Fewest nuisance alerts: AOSU Video Doorbell R1 Ultra. Radar plus PIR plus AI cuts the shadow and car triggers that PIR-only doorbells fire on, it stores 60 days in the base, and it can run on doorbell wiring.
  • Packages on the porch and Home Assistant: eufy Video Doorbell E340. The second, down-facing camera shows the doormat, the battery pack swaps, and it is the only one here Home Assistant users recommend. Budget for a chime and, if you want more than 8 GB, a HomeBase.
  • Dual-band Wi-Fi and a 2-year warranty: Reolink Video Doorbell (Battery). No chime in the box and the card sits in the doorbell.

Not recommended

  • Ring, Nest and Arlo battery doorbells. They are fine hardware, but recorded video needs a monthly plan. They do not answer this question.
  • AOSU Video Doorbell SE. Cheaper, but it has no base: clips stay in the doorbell, it is 2.4 GHz only, and owners at busy doors report recharging every few weeks.
  • Any battery doorbell if your door is far from the router and you will not add a bridge. Weak signal is the top cause of both missed alerts and dead batteries in every forum we read; pick a base-station model or a wired doorbell instead.
